ideas.title: Fewer, findable longs: 3 a week per channel
ideas.hook: Swap 14 unwatched longs a week for 3 built ones, aimed at watch hours
ideas.why: Every long on both channels is at 0-41 views, including the Marble Run Special the Lab pitched (10 views, 1.6% watched after 6 days). Each channel posts 2 longs a day (14 a week). Metricool's 2026 study of 799,718 videos found 2-4 long uploads a week gave the best results per video, and more than 7 a week lowered total monthly views. YouTube's Feb 1, 2027 YPP rules make long-form watch hours the realistic way in: Shorts pay will need 10M Shorts views per 90 days, and new applicants need 8,000 watch hours (Bounce Theory has ~217K views a month and 165 subs).
ideas.impact: Saves ~2 render hours a day across both channels. Goal: first longs above 100 views and some long-form watch hours each week (now ~0). Results aren't guaranteed; the study is correlational.
ideas.script:
1. Approve this, and the R&D Lab edits agents/formats/youtube-lineup.md on its next run: longs only on Mon, Wed and Fri, 1 per channel each day (3 a week, down from 14). On other days the lineup is 15 Shorts only.
2. Paste the build prompt into Claude Code in YOUTUBE HQ so both video skills make a long only when the lineup has one.
3. Each long uses the Long-Form Doctor's L1/L2 advice plus a Lab Long lead ('Escape to a <place>' rain long, an explainer long), and gets 3 title options.
4. When each long goes public, open YouTube Studio and set it as the 'Related video' on that day's 3 strongest Shorts on the same channel, so Shorts viewers have a path to it (manual, ~2 min).
5. Spend the freed render time on Shorts quality.
Risks: fewer uploads can mean fewer chances to get lucky, so keep at least 3 a week.
Check in 2 weeks: the median views per long should be above the 0-41 baseline, and Studio → Earn should show long-form watch hours moving. If not, go back to the old count.

ideas.title: Keyword-first captions for every TikTok
ideas.hook: Fix the caption half of the reach drop in 10 minutes: keyword line, on-screen keyword, one question
ideas.why: TikTok views fell from ~700 to ~250 since Oct 21, and 15 of the last 20 posts end in 'Follow for more' (TikTok reviewer). Metricool's 2026 TikTok study says TikTok reads the first caption line, on-screen text and the transcript to file a video; question captions get 26.19% more comments, and like-CTAs cut likes by ~60%.
ideas.impact: Better topic matching and search reach; realistic goal is getting back to the ~700-view floor within 2 weeks (not guaranteed, since part of the drop may be account-level)
ideas.script:
1. Update the content-scripts skill so every script ends with a caption block: line 1 = the search phrase (e.g. 'stoic advice for young muslim men'), line 2 = one specific question, then 2-4 specific hashtags (no #fyp/#viral).
2. Add an on-screen text cue in scene 1 with the same phrase in the first 3 seconds, and make sure the phrase is said out loud in the first sentence.
3. Ban 'Follow for more' and any 'like if…' line.
4. Turn on auto-captions in TikTok and fix wrong words before posting.
5. Track the next 10 posts in the TikTok reviewer's table: views, comments, search share if shown.
Risk: the drop may be account-level (Oct 21), so captions alone may not fix it; the reviewer should keep watching.
Worked if: the 10 posts after the change average above the ~250 views of the last five, and comments rise.
ideas.buildPrompt: Help me (Omar) update my content-scripts Claude skill for my TikTok self-improvement page (young Muslim guys, Islamic discipline). Problem: my views dropped from ~700 to ~250 per video since Oct 21 and 15 of my last 20 captions end with 'Follow for more'. Evidence from Metricool's 2026 TikTok SEO guide (https://metricool.com/tiktok-seo/): TikTok weighs the first caption line most, reads on-screen text and transcribes speech; question captions got 26.19% more comments; like-CTAs were linked to ~60% fewer likes; use 1-5 specific hashtags, not #fyp/#viral. Change the skill so every script it writes includes: (1) a caption block whose first line is a natural search phrase for the topic, a second line with one specific question, and 2-4 specific hashtags; (2) an on-screen text cue in the first 3 seconds with the same phrase; (3) the phrase spoken in the first sentence; (4) a rule never to write 'Follow for more' or 'like if'. Keep everything else in the skill (scene format, VoicePrint pass, hooks) the same. Also re-create the missing hook-playbook reference file the skill points to, if you can see what it should contain. Show me the full updated SKILL.md so I can save it myself.

ideas.why: A Sept 28, 2026 comparison (Onrec, partner content) puts Etsy review cards at $5-48 one-time and Podium/Birdeye-style platforms at $50-100+/month. ideas.effort: 3h to make the one-pager and test list
ideas.script:

2. One-page offer: 'Tap, review, done. One-time price, no monthly fee', with a price inside the $5-48 Etsy range Omar picks himself.

4. Offer a free 2-week trial stand to 3 shops; count reviews before and after.
Risks: Google rules forbid paying or rewarding for reviews; the stand must not offer discounts for reviews.
Worked if: in 2 weeks 3 trial shops gained reviews and at least 1 paid.

ideas.title: Growth Architect: AI Agent-Powered E-commerce Content Generator
ideas.hook: Automate content creation for Growth Architect clients (e.g., social media posts, product descriptions) using Gemini agents.
ideas.why: Growth Architect's core value is an 'office of AI agents'. This upgrade directly implements a tangible, client-facing agent for content generation, demonstrating the app's power and justifying subscription tiers. This addresses the need to show *specific, actionable marketing plans* and beat generic AI competitors by delivering concrete output for clients. It leverages the free Gemini tier and existing AI tools.
ideas.impact: High - Provides direct, recurring value to small e-commerce clients by automating content creation, which is crucial for client acquisition and retention. Justifies premium tiers ($9.99/$19.99/$39.99).
ideas.cost: $0 (using Gemini free tier for agent logic, free AI tools for output)
ideas.script:
1. **Define Agent Persona & Goal:** Create an 'E-commerce Social Media Content Agent' within Growth Architect. Its goal is to generate 3 engaging social media posts (Instagram/TikTok style) for a new product, given product details, target audience, and desired tone. 
2. **Develop Core Prompt:** Write a robust prompt for this agent, instructing it on how to extract key information and craft posts with hooks, emojis, relevant hashtags, and a clear CTA. 
3. **Integrate Free Content Tools:** Configure the agent to leverage free AI image/video tools (e.g., Krea.ai for abstract visuals or Canva for simple graphics) if visual suggestions are needed, or simply output text.
4. **Test & Refine:** Run the agent with sample product data from a small e-commerce store. Evaluate output quality and refine the prompt until it consistently produces high-quality, actionable content. 
5. **Launch as Feature:** Announce this new agent as a core feature for Growth Architect subscribers, demonstrating its output in marketing materials. Success metric: client feedback on content quality and uptake of the feature in the first 2 weeks.
ideas.buildPrompt:
Paste into Omar's Main Chat in the Claude app
You are an expert in configuring AI agents for e-commerce marketing within the Base44 platform, specifically for the Growth Architect app (app 699b4057d65174480989a52e). Omar needs a step-by-step guide to set up a new 'Social Media Content Generator' agent in Growth Architect. This agent should: 

**Agent Role:** E-commerce Social Media Content Creator
**Agent Goal:** Generate 3 short, engaging social media posts (suitable for Instagram/TikTok) for a new e-commerce product.
**Inputs:** Product Name, Key Features, Target Audience, Desired Tone (e.g., playful, luxurious, practical).
**Output:** 3 distinct social media posts, each including:
    - A strong hook
    - Key product benefits/features
    - Relevant emojis
    - Relevant hashtags
    - A clear call to action (e.g., 'Shop Now!', 'Link in Bio')

Also, suggest how to integrate a placeholder for visual content if the agent cannot directly generate images/videos (e.g., 'Suggested Visual: [description of visual]').

ideas.title: LinkedAI: Personalized Outreach Message Generator
ideas.hook: Generate highly personalized LinkedIn outreach messages for free users, increasing conversion to Pro.
ideas.why: LinkedAI's competitive advantage lies in authentic AI and common ground. This upgrade directly enhances that by providing immediate, tangible value to free users, showcasing the power of personalized AI outreach and differentiating from generic AI tools. This addresses the pain point of generic AI content and helps justify paid tiers.
ideas.impact: High - Increases value for free users, potentially converting them to paid tiers, and improves user experience by delivering highly relevant, personalized content. Estimated 5-10% increase in freemium to paid conversion.
ideas.script: 1. **Integrate Gemini API:** Add a call to the Gemini free tier API within the LinkedAI Chrome extension's codebase. 2. **UI Button:** Implement a 'Generate Outreach Message' button on the LinkedIn profile view. 3. **Data Extraction:** Configure the extension to pull public information from the displayed LinkedIn profile (name, current role, company, recent posts/activity if available). 4. **AI Generation:** Send the extracted data to the Gemini API with a specific prompt to generate a personalized, professional outreach message. 5. **Display Message:** Show the generated message to the user in a pop-up or text area for easy copying and editing. 6. **Testing:** Test on 10 diverse LinkedIn profiles to ensure message quality and relevance. Success will be measured by user feedback and A/B testing on conversion rates to Pro.
ideas.buildPrompt:
Paste into Omar's Main Chat in the Claude app
As an AI assistant, I need to integrate a 'Personalized Outreach Message Generator' feature into the LinkedAI Chrome extension. This feature will use the Gemini free tier API. Please provide the step-by-step instructions, including code snippets for JavaScript (for the Chrome extension) and API calls (for Gemini), to:
1. Add a button to the LinkedIn profile page (e.g., next to the 'Connect' button).
2. When clicked, extract public information from the current LinkedIn profile (name, current job title, company, and ideally, a summary of their recent activity or skills).
3. Send this information to the Gemini API to generate a personalized connection request message. The message should be concise, respectful, professional, and explicitly state a relevant reason for connecting (e.g., 'to learn from your insights on [topic]' or 'to discuss shared interests in [skill]'). Ensure it does not sound salesy or generic.
4. Display the generated message in a user-friendly format (e.g., a modal or text area) within the extension for the user to copy/edit.
Assume the user has already granted necessary LinkedIn profile access permissions to the extension. Name any specific files in the LinkedAI repo (e.g., `content.js`, `popup.html`, `background.js`) that would need modification.

ideas.why: LinkedAI users need instant, tailored outreach without complex setup. Competitor analysis shows users churn when AI prompts feel too open-ended or require long prompt writing.
ideas.impact: Increases daily extension retention and conversion from free to Pro by giving immediate utility on first install.
ideas.script: 1. Add a dropdown of 5 structured outreach intents (Alumni, Hiring Manager, Peer, Recruiter, Founder) into the extension popup. 2. When clicked, pull the target profile's current role and company name to fill a tight 280-character template without inventing background details. 3. Provide an edit box so the user reviews and confirms before sending. 4. Track click-through rate over 14 days to confirm higher message generation volume.
